findings.location: crates/foundry-app/static/css/foundry.b3a70ff6.css:1006 (overflow-y: auto on the bare .sidebar rule), against css:1114-1119 and css:1136-1149 (the folded flyout) ; prescribed by docs/feature/ui-nav-polish/architecture.md:288 and risk Y5
findings.obligation: The shipped nav-collapse-icon-rail promise: while the nav is narrow, each icon shows the name of the place it opens in a box beside it when the operator hovers it or reaches it with the Tab key. The design states the sticky-rail change is adapter-only and breaks no shipped promise, and Y5 names overflow-y: auto as the very mechanism that keeps every member reachable.
findings.observation: The new declaration makes .sidebar a scroll container. CSS Overflow Module Level 3 section 3 computes overflow-x from visible to auto whenever the other axis is not visible or clip, so the rail now clips its scrollable overflow on BOTH axes. In the folded desk geometry the rail is 72px wide (css:1055-1058), each member is position: relative (css:1088) and the revealed word is position: absolute, left: 100%, margin-left: 8px (css:1114-1119), so the flyout box lies entirely outside the rail padding box and is now clipped out of view instead of overflowing past the rail edge; nothing scrolls the rail horizontally to bring it back. NO READING IN THE CANDIDATE OR IN ANY SHIPPED LANE CAN SEE THIS: the flyout assertion (feature_nav_icon_rail.rs:591-671) compares the label LAYOUT box while focused against the layout box while unfocused, and an ancestor overflow leaves a layout box untouched - the step module says so itself at lines 576-584 - while its hit test at the label centre is recorded (labelCentreHitsTheLabel) and deliberately not asserted. The candidate P3 rows read the rail box and the members, never the revealed word. CAPABILITY LIMIT, STATED: the reviewer did NOT measure this in a browser; it is derived from the stylesheet bytes and the normative overflow rule, and the host green run cannot refute it because no assertion reads the clipped flyout.
findings.remediation: Decide the mechanism that keeps the rail in view WITHOUT making it clip its own flyout, and have a reading observe the choice. Either scope the scroll container so the flyout is not clipped (for example overflow-y: auto only where the rail is taller than the window, or move the revealed word inside the rail box), or keep overflow and have the acceptance designer add one row that reads the revealed word as VISIBLE in the folded geometry (the clip-aware visible test support/rail_reading.rs already owns, not the layout box). Measure it in the browser lane before closing: open the folded rail at desk width, focus a member and read whether the centre of the revealed box hit-tests back to the word.

findings.location: crates/foundry-app/templates/partials/sidebar.html:72-73 together with crates/foundry-app/src/nav.rs:168-207 (invites_for, tokens_for) ; declared state docs/feature/ui-nav-polish/architecture.md Admitted "Identity lookup failed ... the page still renders 200 with Home marked" and failure B1
findings.obligation: L1 and claim C1: on every authenticated page a signed-in operator can open, EXACTLY ONE primary nav member carries aria-current=page, never zero; and the shipped navigation-bar-linear-ui promise asserts the same. The design declares for failure B1 that a render whose identity lookup failed still marks the page family it is on and offers neither admin link.
findings.observation: On /workspace/invites and /admin/tokens the two obligations meet on the SAME member and contradict each other. The handler names NavSection::Invites or NavSection::Tokens before and independently of the identity resolution, while the template renders that member only inside {% if nav.is_workspace_admin %}. When the route gate has already admitted a workspace admin but the separate nav_identity read fails for that render, the neutral identity reports is_workspace_admin false, the marked member is not rendered at all, and every other member answers its predicate false - so the served rail carries ZERO aria-current. That is the state C1 says is unrepresentable and the state the shipped exactly-one-current promise forbids, and it is not what the design declares for B1 (Home marked). The carrier itself is sound; the deviation is in the composition of P1 and P2 on the two conditional members. Reachability: only through the declared B1 failure branch, whose acceptance row is recorded NotTested with owner solution-architect because no public surface makes the lookup fail, so no lane observes it and the host green run says nothing about it.
findings.remediation: Close the composition rather than the symptom: either resolve the section inside resolved() so a page whose member the rail will not offer falls back to NavSection::Home - which makes the rendered rail satisfy both L1 and L2 on the failure branch and matches the declared B1 outcome - or amend the declared B1 state, L1 and C1 to say that a rail rendered from a neutral identity on an admin page carries no mark, and record that the shipped exactly-one-current promise is then bounded to renders whose identity resolved. Name which of the two the user accepts; do not leave the record and the code disagreeing.
